Edmund Burke reacted to the political issues of the day.
Horrified by the extremes of the French Revolution, Burke used these as an example of the flaws of following the values of equality, individualism, and freedom.
Burke believed that established institutions, run by the educated people of society, were necessary to control the irrational passions of the uneducated masses.
According to Burke, the only reason to make changes to these institutions was to preserve them from the radical or revolutionary change demanded by the masses.
